transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14 15:30 UTC
Duration: 36 minutes
Attendees: Carlos Mendes (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam Zhou (Redwood CSM), Ellen Kim (CTO, Lighthouse AI), Jordan Reyes (ML Eng), Samir Patel (Platform), Olivia Park (Security)

[00:00] Carlos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Carlos with Redwood, this is Priya our SE and Liam from CS. Quick high level, we want to run through the PLG quickstart, free credits, and understand your time-to-first-token goals. Ellen, do you want to kick off with where you are?
[00:22] Ellen: Yeah thanks, Carlos. We're building a customer-facing summarization feature inside Lighthouse's dashboard. Right now using a homegrown LLM stack but it's getting expensive to maintain. We're interested in a hosted API first to move faster, but long term may need dedicated capacity because of PII and latency.
[00:45] Jordan: +1. We need low latency for interactive sessions, also curious about cost per token and how batching might affect our UX.
[01:10] Priya: Great, that's helpful. For PLG quickstart we usually get teams to create an account, claim free credits, and run a small sample to get time-to-first-token under 15 minutes. The quickstart includes curl and SDK snippets. Do you all have SSO or any enterprise constraints today?
[01:38] Olivia: We use Okta SAML and have SOC2 in progress. Also strong KMS requirements - we manage keys via AWS KMS for production. How does Redwood handle KMS and key access for hosted customers?
[02:05] Liam: Good question - Redwood hosted supports customer-managed keys via integrations with major KMS providers; for Private we support full customer-managed key controls. We'll share the security whitepaper after this.
[02:28] Samir: For Dedicated, what's the difference in isolation? Is it just tenant separation or network-level VPC?
[02:45] Priya: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and a VPC-like network isolation; there's also options for private control plane if you need it on-prem. There's a tradeoff between cost and manageability.
[03:12] Ellen: Any benchmarks around latency for the smaller open models versus, say, Anthropic or OpenAI hosted endpoints? We want to compare predictably.
[03:30] Priya: We publish model profiles - for hosted quickstart we usually suggest a small open model to validate flows. For production you can switch to a quantized variant or a higher perfserv model. Benchmarks depend a lot on sequence length and batching. We'll send our model catalog link.
[03:58] Jordan: How fast can we realistically expect first inference? Our prototype is about 400ms for a short prompt; we need under 1s in the dashboard.
[04:18] Priya: For short prompts on hosted, sub-second is typical for many models, but it depends on load and routing. Quickstart will show you end-to-end from sign-up to token in ~10 minutes if you follow the snippet. There might be slight transcription in logs - sorry I mean jitter - during peak.
[04:45] Carlos: Also worth noting we do continuous batching and KV cache for conversational flows, which can reduce cost and improve p99 latency for repeated prefixes.
[05:06] Ellen: Can you explain KV cache? I sometimes see it written K-V cash in our docs and it's confusing.
[05:20] Priya: Sure - KV cache is kernel value cache, it's the model's attention cache to avoid recomputing tokens. Good for chat-style UIs.
[05:42] Jordan: On the security side, we need audit logs and data retention controls. Are logs accessible per-route and per-token?
[05:58] Liam: Redwood Console provides per-route latency/cost breakdowns and tracing hooks. Audit logs and retention are configurable; we'll include screenshots in the doc we'll send.
[06:20] Olivia: Any concerns about PII leaving region? We need EU data residency for EU customers. Hosted options - can you pin region?
[06:37] Priya: Hosted can route to region-specific clusters; for strict residency Dedicated or Private is recommended. We'll discuss region pins in the deep dive.
[07:00] Carlos: Let's walk through a quickstart flow - I'll share the quickstart link in chat and Priya will run through the curl snippet.
[07:15] Priya: Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"summarize: ..."}' - you'll get a JSON with tokens and streaming options.
[07:48] Jordan: Do you provide SDKs? We use Python and Node.
[07:53] Priya: Yes, official SDKs for Python, Node, and community examples. SDK includes streaming helpers and structured output parsing.
[08:10] Ellen: About free credits - what's typical for PLG trials? We want enough to validate flows and run some perf tests.
[08:20] Carlos: We can provision an initial $500 free credits for teams doing quickstarts; that usually covers early dev and perf runs. We'll attach the redemption link.
[08:35] Samir: Great. For evaluating Dedicated later, what's the typical timeline for provisioning reserved capacity?
[08:45] Priya: Dedicated lead times vary but often a few weeks depending on scale and region. We usually do a POC with a small reserved pool.
[09:00] Jordan: Any gotchas with switching from hosted to dedicated mid-project? We want minimal code changes.
[09:10] Priya: We expose a consistent API and routing layer so code changes are minimal - mostly config changes to endpoint and keys, and perhaps model pinning. Some infra tests recommended though.
[09:30] Ellen: On compliance, can you share SOC2 report and pen test summaries?
[09:38] Liam: We'll share SOC2 docs and a security checklist. For Private installs, there are add-on compliance packs.
[09:55] Olivia: What about SSO and RBAC? We need role separation for dev vs prod keys.
[10:05] Priya: RBAC and SSO (Okta, SAML) supported; keys can be scoped by team/route. We'll include an RBAC example.
[10:28] Carlos: Quick question on pricing cadence - is hosted billed per token and embeddings?
[10:36] Carlos: (continues) We have usage-based pricing per token and per embedding unit; Dedicated is committed monthly capacity with reserved GPU pools. Pricing examples will be in the doc.
[10:55] Jordan: For cost optimization, what tooling do you provide?
[11:02] Priya: Redwood Optimize suggests batching/caching and quantization profiles; we also surface token-level cost breakdowns in the Console.
[11:22] Ellen: We might need a short perf test to compare our in-house runtimes vs Redwood. Can Redwood run a small benchmark for us or do we run it?
[11:34] Priya: Both. We can provide a benchmark spreadsheet and scripts; if you want we'll run a Redwood-hosted benchmark against your sample prompts as well.
[11:50] Samir: For the benchmark, we care about 95th and 99th percentile latency and cost per 1k requests.
[12:00] Priya: Noted. We'll include fields for p95/p99 and cost.
[12:12] Carlos: Any competitors you are evaluating?
[12:16] Ellen: We're looking at Anthropic and OpenAI for hosted APIs, and ModelServe for self-hosted.
[12:25] Priya: Good to know.
[12:35] Jordan: Operationally, how do you handle model rollouts and fallback? If a model has a regression, can we auto-fallback to an older variant?
[12:45] Priya: Yes - Redwood supports rollouts, canary deploys, and automatic fallback to pinned variants. Eval-based regression alerts are also supported.
[13:04] Ellen: Can you walk me through a sample quickstart timeline so I can share with my PM?
[13:12] Carlos: Sure: Day 0 - sign up and claim credits, Day 1 - run quickstart and validate time-to-first-token, Day 2-5 - integrate SDK and run perf tests, Week 2 - schedule dedicated scoping if needed.
[13:35] Jordan: Sounds reasonable. For the quickstart, is there any support from Redwood or is it self-serve?
[13:42] Liam: It's PLG-first but we provide quickstart guides and can offer SE office hours for teams that need help.
[13:58] Ellen: Great. Olivia, any security blockers on moving forward with a hosted trial?
[14:06] Olivia: As long as we get SOC2 and KMS integration details and assurance on audit logs, we can start the hosted trial. For production we'll evaluate Dedicated or Private.
[14:22] Carlos: Perfect. We'll send the quickstart link, credit redemption, SOC2 and KMS docs, and schedule the SE deep dive next week.
[14:35] Priya: I'll take lead on the technical session, we'll propose times.
[14:45] Ellen: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[15:00] Carlos: Thanks - recap: Carlos to send quickstart + credits, Priya to schedule deep-dive, Liam to share SOC2 docs. Any final Qs?
[15:12] Olivia: No, that's it.
[15:20] Ellen: Looking forward to trying the quickstart.
[15:28] Carlos: Great - we'll follow up via email and slack.

Notes: transcript includes occasional minor mis-transcriptions and filler words consistent with automatic transcription. References to KV cache/K-V cash and kernel value explanation reflect typical SE clarifications.

End of call.
